## Summary

**Context:** This is `page-assist`, a browser-extension chat client where end users bring their own provider API keys (stored in IndexedDB via Settings UI) for OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Ollama, OpenRouter, etc. A prior deterministic codemod already added a vendored runtime (`src/lib/routerRuntime.ts`) that transparently reroutes `api.openai.com` and `api.anthropic.com` traffic to Router when the build sets `RAMP_ROUTER_API_KEY`, leaving everything else (other providers, embeddings, audio, model-listing) untouched. It had already wired this into three sites:

- `src/models/CustomChatOpenAI.ts` (OpenAI Chat Completions client)
- `src/models/OAIEmbedding.ts` (embeddings — inert since Router has no embeddings endpoint)
- `src/services/openai-tts.ts` (TTS — inert since Router has no audio endpoint)

**What I migrated:** The one remaining gap, flagged in `.router-migrate/HANDOFF.md`: `src/models/CustomChatAnthropic.ts:355` made a raw `fetch("https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages", ...)` call that bypassed the runtime entirely. I changed it to route through `routerFetch()`:

```ts
const doFetch = routerFetch() ?? fetch
const response = await doFetch("https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages", { ... })
```

This preserves the existing Anthropic Messages request/response shape (correct per the instructions — Router's Messages-compatible surface doesn't need a Responses rewrite), keeps behavior byte-identical when `RAMP_ROUTER_API_KEY` is unset, and when set, redirects to `{router}/v1/messages` with only the Router bearer key (the user's own `x-api-key` never reaches Router — confirmed with a bundled esbuild sanity test that captured the outgoing request).

**Verified:**
- `tsc --noEmit` shows only pre-existing, unrelated baseline errors (mcp.tsx, get-html.ts, get-tab-contents.ts, wxt.config.ts) — none touching the changed file.
- Router simulator run (`sim_test.py`) matches baseline (same exit code 2, 0 requests/0 rejected — expected since the test suite here is typecheck-only and makes no live calls).
- Standalone esbuild-bundled test against a mocked `fetch` confirmed the Anthropic request is correctly rewritten to Router's `/v1/messages`, the dated model id `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` resolves to catalog id `claude-sonnet-4-5`, and the provider key is dropped.

**Call sites I could not migrate / intentionally left unchanged** (all already documented as "kept" in the prior codemod's report, confirmed still accurate):
- `src/models/OAIEmbedding.ts:159` (`embeddings.create`) — Router has no `/v1/embeddings` endpoint.
- `src/services/openai-tts.ts:27` (`audio.speech.create`) — Router has no audio endpoints.
- `src/libs/openai.ts:43` (`getAllAnthropicModels`, raw `GET /v1/models`) — this lists the *user's own* provider account's models for the Settings dropdown, not generation traffic; Router's `GET /v1/models` lists Router's own catalog and serves a different purpose, so rewriting this would change behavior, not just transport.
- `src/models/ChatGoogleAI.ts` (Gemini via OpenAI-compatible endpoint) — hits `generativelanguage.googleapis.com`, a host Router's catalog doesn't serve; wrapping it would be a no-op.
- All other providers (Ollama, Chrome built-in AI, OpenRouter, Vertex via custom base URLs, Together, etc.) are unaffected by design — the runtime only intercepts the literal `api.openai.com`/`api.anthropic.com` hosts, matching how the other already-migrated call sites behave.
